item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Update to EWS Access for Kiosk / Frontline Worker Licenses
item.description:
Updated October 16, 2026: We have decided not to move forward with this change. We apologize for any inconvenience. 

We're making some changes to Exchange Web Services (EWS).

Starting October 1, 2026 (previously June 30), we will start to block EWS access for all mailboxes without license rights to EWS. This is another step in our ongoing commitment to enhance the security and control mechanisms of EWS.

[How this will affect your organization:]

The impacted licenses are:

  • Exchange Online Kiosk
  • Microsoft 365 and Office 365 F1
  • Microsoft 365 and Office 365 F3

As stated in the Service Descriptions, these licenses do not provide access to mailboxes via EWS, but these restrictions were never enforced. With this change, EWS access for users with only these license types will be blocked.

[What you need to do to prepare:]

If you wish these users to continue to use EWS, and your users are licensed with one of these noted above, you’ll need to assign a new license, one containing EWS access rights. For example, you could assign an Exchange Online Plan 1 or 2 license, or a Microsoft 365 or Office 365 E3 or E5 license.

Starting October 1, 2026 (previously June 30), requests to use EWS without a suitable license will result in a HTTP 403 response.

Learn more: Update to EWS Access for Kiosk / Frontline Worker Licensed Users

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 admin center: New usage report for Copilot connectors
item.description:
Updated October 16, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[Introduction]

To help administrators better understand and manage adoption of Copilot connectors, Microsoft is introducing a new Copilot connectors usage report in the Microsoft 365 admin center. This report provides visibility into how connectors are used across Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences, helping organizations assess adoption, identify usage patterns, and optimize connector deployment.

This update supports customer feedback requesting clearer reporting on Copilot connector usage across entry points such as Copilot Chat, Search, and agents.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 519571.

[When this will happen:]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out late June 2026 and expect to complete by early July 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out November 2026 (previously late September) and expect to complete November 2026 (previously end of September).

[How this affects your organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Microsoft 365 administrators
  • Organizations using Copilot connectors with the Microsoft 365 Copilot app
  • A Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) license is required to use this feature

What will happen:

  • A new “Connectors” report will appear in Microsoft 365 admin center under Reporting > Usage > Microsoft 365 Copilot > Connectors.
  • The report will show:
    • Active users of connectors across Copilot Chat, Copilot Search, and agents
    • Total connector responses generated in the organization
    • Daily trend views of active usage and total responses
    • Usage breakdown per user and per connector
  • The report is enabled by default and respects existing permissions.
  • There is no impact to user workflows.

[What you can do to prepare:]

No action is required before rollout.

  • Inform relevant administrators and analytics stakeholders about the new report.
  • Review the report after rollout to assess Copilot connector adoption and usage trends.
  • Update internal documentation if Copilot reporting is referenced.

Learn more: Copilot connectors usage report documentation

[Compliance considerations:]

This change introduces a new admin usage report that improves visibility into Copilot connector usage. No other compliance considerations are impacted.

item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] (Updated) Windows updates are available for 2026 time zone changes in Canada
item.description:
(Updated October 16, 2026: Added guidance for managing the Alberta and British Columbia time zone changes in Outlook Time Zone Changes for Alberta and British Columbia.)

What and why

Windows updates are now available to support the 2026 time zone changes in Manitoba, Alberta, and British Columbia. On November 1, 2026, clocks in affected regions will not be set back by one hour.

Manitoba will permanently stay on UTC-5, Alberta and affected locations will permanently stay on UTC-6, and most of British Columbia will permanently stay on UTC-7. The new Windows updates add region-specific time zones to support these changes.

Rollout schedule

  • September 22, 2026: The Alberta and British Columbia changes became available in the September 2026 non-security preview update for Windows 11, versions 25H2 and 24H2.
  • October 13, 2026: The Manitoba change became available for all supported versions of Windows. The Alberta and British Columbia changes became available for all other supported versions of Windows, including Windows Server. These changes are included in the October 2026 security update.
  • November 1, 2026: The time zone transitions take effect at 2:00 a.m. local time. Clocks in affected areas will not be set back by one hour.

Impact on your organization

Devices in affected regions will display an incorrect local time after the November 1, 2026 transition if the applicable Windows update is not installed or the appropriate time zone is not selected. The updates add the following region-specific time zones:

  • (UTC-05:00) Manitoba 
  • (UTC-06:00) Mountain Time (Alberta)
  • (UTC-07:00) Pacific Time (British Columbia)

The Alberta time zone change also applies to Yellowknife and Inuvik in the Northwest Territories and locations in southeastern British Columbia that align with Alberta.

Devices configured to set the time zone automatically will select the appropriate new time zone. On other devices, the new region-specific time zone must be selected manually.

Action required/recommendations

  • Install the applicable Windows update on affected devices before November 1, 2026.
  • Confirm that affected devices use the appropriate region-specific time zone after installing the update.
  • If a device cannot receive the update before November 1, 2026, read and follow the interim guidance for each affected region detailed in the Daylight Saving Time & Time Zone Blog and move the device to the appropriate region-specific time zone as soon as possible.

Note: To manage this change in Outlook, please follow the guidance in the article Outlook Time Zone Changes for Alberta and British Columbia.

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations are identified. Review as appropriate for your organization and region-specific time zone.

Additional information

  • Daylight Saving Time & Time Zone Blog
  • Alberta 2026 time zone update available now
  • British Columbia 2026 time zone update available now
  • Manitoba 2026 time zone update available now
  • Outlook Time Zone Changes for Alberta and British Columbia | Microsoft Support
  • Daylight saving time help and support

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot for Teams: Bilingual consecutive interpretation mode with Interpreter agent
item.description:
Updated July 13, 2026: We have paused rollout of this feature at this time. We will provide an update via Message center when we are ready to proceed. We apologize for any inconvenience. 

[Introduction]

Consecutive Interpretation is a new interpretation mode available as an add‑on to the existing Interpreter agent in Microsoft Teams. It enables structured multilingual conversations in meetings by providing shared, meeting‑level interpretation when enabled by a Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed user.

This mode uses consecutive (turn‑by‑turn) interpretation, meaning participants speak one at a time and each speaker's words are interpreted before the next speaker begins. This structured flow reduces overlap, improves interpretation accuracy, and helps everyone stay aligned in real time.

Consecutive Interpretation is ideal for back‑and‑forth, interactive discussions where participants need to respond, clarify, and build on each other’s input across languages, such as working sessions, negotiations, and cross‑functional collaboration.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 557180.

[When this will happen]

  • Targeted Release: Rollout begins in early May 2026 (previously early April) and is expected to complete by late May 2026 (previously mid-April).
  • General Availability (Worldwide): We will provide an update via Message center when we are ready to proceed.

[How this will affect your organization]

Who is affected

  • All Microsoft 365 tenants using Microsoft Teams meetings where users are licensed with Microsoft 365 Copilot.

What will happen

  • For tenants
    • The new Consecutive Interpretation mode extends the existing Interpreter agent to support structured, interactive multilingual meetings.
    • The existing Interpreter experience remains unchanged unless this new mode is enabled.
  • For admins
    • No new tenant‑level configuration is required.
    • The feature is available to all users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
    • Existing compliance, privacy, and data‑handling policies for Interpreter continue to apply.
  • For users
    • When a Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed user enables the mode, interpretation becomes a shared meeting‑level experience rather than an individual setting.
    • Participants speak consecutively, with each turn interpreted and delivered before the next participant begins.

[What you need to do to prepare]

  • No action is required to maintain current behavior.
  • Ensure any users who intend to use this mode have an active Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • Consider providing guidance to users about when this mode is best suited (for example, working sessions, negotiations, or detailed multilingual collaboration).

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365: Enrich profile cards with custom properties from third-party systems

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Copilot Notebooks: Suggested artifacts for faster content creation
item.description:
Updated October 16, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and Why:]

Copilot Notebooks will intelligently recommend relevant artifacts based on your Microsoft 365 knowledge and the content in your notebook, helping you move work forward faster without leaving the notebook experience. By automatically leveraging existing context and background information, Copilot reduces the need to repeatedly write prompts containing the same details when creating new content from notebook materials. Supported artifact types include Word documents, Excel workbooks, and PowerPoint presentations. Support for additional artifact types, including PDFs and Pages, will be introduced in a future release.

This message is associated with Roadmap ID 566870.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): Beginning in early July 2026; expected to complete by late August 2026.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in late August 2026; (previously late July) expected to complete by early November 2026 (previously late September).

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who can currently create artifacts within Copilot Notebooks.
  • Organizations licensed for Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) with access to Copilot Notebooks.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Copilot Notebooks
  • Word
  • Excel
  • PowerPoint

What will happen:

  • Users will see proactive artifact recommendations within Copilot Notebooks.
  • Suggestions are generated using notebook references, pages, and Microsoft 365 context.
  • Supported artifact types include Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
  • Future releases are expected to add support for PDFs and Pages.
  • The feature is available by default for eligible users.
  • No admin configuration is required.

Screenshot - Copilot Notebooks screen with recommended artifacts

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required.

We recommend that you:

  • Review user-facing communications regarding Copilot Notebooks.
  • Inform help desk teams about the new recommendation experience.
  • Update internal training and adoption materials as appropriate.
  • Monitor roadmap communications for future artifact type support.

[Compliance Considerations:]

Compliance considerationExplanation
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Artifact suggestions are generated using content already available in Copilot Notebooks, including notebook references, pages, and the user's Microsoft 365 context. This introduces additional AI-driven processing of existing customer data to determine relevant artifact recommendations.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?The feature adds proactive AI-generated artifact recommendations that analyze notebook content and Microsoft 365 context to suggest next-step deliverables such as Word documents, Excel workbooks, and PowerPoint presentations.
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Users can receive contextual artifact recommendations directly within Copilot Notebooks and generate content from pre-populated prompts that incorporate relevant notebook information.
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?The announcement does not specify whether recommendation activity will be surfaced in existing audit, reporting, or compliance experiences. Organizations may wish to review future documentation for additional compliance-related details.
Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?No new administrative controls are described. The feature appears to be available to users who already have permission to create artifacts in Copilot Notebooks, but Microsoft has not explicitly documented control mechanisms.
Does the change allow a user to enable and disable the feature themselves?The announcement states that users remain in control of whether they use suggested artifacts, but it does not specify whether the recommendation experience itself can be enabled or disabled by individual users.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Teams: Upcoming change to voicemail message delivery by email
item.description:
[What and why]

We’re changing how Microsoft Teams voicemail messages are delivered by email to improve security and give organizations more control over sender identity. Organizations will be able to send voicemail notifications from their own domain and apply existing SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and domain-protection policies to help prevent spoofing and impersonation.

Supporting organization-owned sending domains requires a new voicemail email delivery solution. Caller information will move from the email From field to the Subject line and remain in the message body.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout is currently estimated to begin in early March 2027 and complete by late June 2027.
    • Note: This schedule is subject to change. We will publish an updated Message center communication with the confirmed rollout timeline and required customer actions.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations that are using Teams Calling.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Voicemail
  • Exchange Online

What will happen

  • The From field in voicemail email messages will no longer contain the caller’s name, phone number, or email address.
  • The sender address will support Bring Your Own Domain (BYOD), allowing organizations to use their own domain for voicemail email delivery.
  • Caller information will move to the Subject line and remain in the message body.
  • Organizations should review and prepare to update mail-flow rules, allowlists, filtering, routing, or automation based on the current voicemail sender identity or domain.
  • Caller information will continue to appear in Teams as it does today, while the underlying email delivery and sender domain will change.

item.title: [planForChange] Action required: Review property changes for Exchange Online scenarios
item.description:
[What and why:]

As part of our ongoing Exchange Online management and directory modernization efforts, we're simplifying legacy management scenarios and removing properties. We are deprecating selected properties returned or used with the following Exchange Online PowerShell scenarios:

  • Get-Mailbox -Migration
  • New-Mailbox -Migration

If your scripts, applications, or automation use these scenarios, review the affected properties and determine whether your workflows depend on them.

The change will be introduced in two phases:

  • Beginning November 15, 2026: Selected properties will no longer be returned in applicable Get-Mailbox -Migration and New-Mailbox -Migration responses.
  • Beginning December 15, 2026: The affected properties will be blocked from being configured through applicable New-Mailbox -Migration scenarios.

[Rollout schedule:]

We will begin rolling out mid-November 2026 and expect to complete by mid-November 2026.

[Impact on your organization:]

Your organization may be affected if you have scripts, applications, third-party solutions, or operational workflows that use the affected properties with -Migration scenarios.

For example, a script using: Get-Mailbox -Migration will no longer receive the affected properties in the returned object beginning November 10, 2026. This may affect automation that depends on those properties being present or expects a fixed set of properties in the response. If your workflows don't use any of the affected properties, no action is required.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

Before November 15, 2026:

  1. Review scripts, applications, and integrations that use Get-Mailbox -Migration, New-Mailbox -Migration, or Set-Mailbox -Migration.
  2. Review the published list of affected properties.
  3. Identify whether your workflows depend on any affected property.
  4. Update and test affected workflows to remove the dependency.
  5. For the complete list of affected properties and additional guidance, see: Changes to Get-Mailbox and New-Mailbox specifically with the Migration parameter | Microsoft Learn.

Required Actions

Review your -Migration workflows and make any required changes before November 15, 2026.

If an affected property is required for your scenario and you can't remove the dependency, contact Microsoft Support and provide the property name, cmdlet, usage scenario, and expected impact.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Copilot Studio – Teams app retirement
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft is continuing the transition of Copilot Studio experiences from the Microsoft Teams app to the Copilot Studio web app at https://copilotstudio.microsoft.com/.

Users can continue to create, edit, publish, and manage classic-style chatbot agents in the Copilot Studio web app. Agent creation in the Teams app is already no longer supported. Beginning in January 2027, editing agents in the Teams app will no longer be supported. Beginning in February 2027, the Copilot Studio app will no longer be available in Microsoft Teams.

[Rollout Schedule:]

We will begin rolling out in early January 2027 and expect to complete by early February 2027.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who currently use the Copilot Studio app in Microsoft Teams to create, edit, publish, or manage classic-style chatbot agents.
  • Admins and support teams who provide guidance for Copilot Studio agent management.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft Copilot Studio
  • Microsoft Teams
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen:

  • Users can continue to manage supported classic-style agents in the Copilot Studio web app.
  • Starting in January 2027, editing existing agents in the Copilot Studio app within Microsoft Teams will no longer be supported.
  • Starting in February 2027, the Copilot Studio app will be removed from Microsoft Teams and will no longer be available.
  • Users should use the Copilot Studio web app for supported agent creation, editing, publishing, and management experiences.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  • Inform affected users that Copilot Studio agent management should move to the Copilot Studio web app.
  • Update internal documentation, training, and support guidance that references the Copilot Studio app in Microsoft Teams.
  • Review any bookmarks, user communications, or helpdesk scripts that direct users to manage agents from Teams.
  • Direct users to https://copilotstudio.microsoft.com/ for supported Copilot Studio web experiences.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Upcoming changes to Agents in SharePoint and OneDrive
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We are upgrading the agent experience in SharePoint and OneDrive to better align with the Microsoft Copilot extensibility ecosystem, specifically to ensure that these agents are part of Copilot app home experiences (MC1479277) and the Microsoft plugin registry (MC1484008), the shared catalog for discovering, publishing, and governing organization-approved and custom-built plugins across Microsoft Copilot experiences (Chat, Cowork, Code, Autopilot) and Microsoft 365 apps (Word, PowerPoint, Excel), OneDrive and SharePoint. 

Agents using .agent file format will continue to work across SharePoint, Teams, and Copilot app until the end of March 2027. With upcoming updates, agent owners can start upgrading each experience. The right path depends on what each agent helps users accomplish today: 

  1. Use Copilot in SharePoint for site-level questions and answers.
  2. Convert the .agent file to a skill for Copilot in SharePoint when it supports a focused task or business outcome specific to the site.
  3. Upgrade to a declarative agent or update your custom engine agent that was published to the SharePoint channel, when users need a content-grounded, conversational experience across Microsoft 365.

Changes to agent creation and building experiences in OneDrive and SharePoint will support this transition:

  • Creating agents will use the Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder
  • An Upgrade button will appear in the SharePoint builder so you can upgrade the agent to use the Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder. 
  • A convert-agent-file-to-skill skill will be available in Copilot in SharePoint

Changes to the user experience of the site will support this transition:

  • The Agent Chat web part is coming soon to allow any agent from the Plugin store to appear on the SharePoint site with more intention and control for greater reach and impact
  • Copilot in SharePoint is already available worldwide and is coming soon to Government clouds.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide and Government clouds): This change consists of two rollouts:

  • Agent creation and upgrade: Rollout begins mid-November and is expected to complete by early December 2026
  • Agents in SharePoint and OneDrive using .agent file format stop working in SharePoint, Teams and Copilot app: Rollout begins early April and is expected to complete mid-April 2027

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Organizations using agents in SharePoint and OneDrive.
  • SharePoint site owners and members who create or manage agents in the .agent file format.
  • Admins responsible for agent governance, adoption, licensing, and support.

Platforms/Services:

  • SharePoint
  • OneDrive
  • Copilot in SharePoint
  • Microsoft 365 agents
  • Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder
  • Microsoft Plugin store

What will happen:

Beginning mid-November, users no longer create agents in the .agent file format, and features to support upgrading .agent files will be available. 

  • Creating agents will use the Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder and appear in Plugin store.
  • An Upgrade button appears in the SharePoint builder.
  • A convert-agent-file-to-skill skill is available in Copilot in SharePoint
  • Upgraded agents must be re-added to Teams Chat/Channel
  • With Agent Chat web part, site owners/page authors can add any agent from the Plugin store into SharePoint.

After March 2027, agents using .agent file format will stop working in SharePoint, Teams and Copilot app; including Agent Link web part, immersive experience, chat pane in SharePoint.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Begin preparing for the transition away from SharePoint and OneDrive .agent files now. Identify the teams that own or manage agents, share the March 2027 deadline, and ensure that site and agent owners understand the upgrade paths. Administrators should become familiar with Copilot in SharePoint, Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder, Agent 365 and the governance and management capabilities that will apply to upgraded experiences. 

You don’t need to change any .agent file format agents today, but the following changes will help you transition:

  1. “Create an agent”/“New agent” in SharePoint/OneDrive open Microsoft Copilot Agent Builder for creation. These agents are added to the Plugin store and will not create .agent files. 
  2. You can continue to edit existing .agent files during the transition period. When you are ready to upgrade, use the Upgrade to M365 Agent button in the SharePoint agent builder or convert-agent-file-to-skill skill in Copilot in SharePoint. 
  3. Use the Agent Chat web part to add the agent to a SharePoint page.

Review the guidance on finding and upgrading existing agents.

[Compliance considerations:]

Does the change store new customer data, if so, where, and is the data cached or permanently stored?Yes. Upgraded and new agents managed through the Agent Builder, Plugin store, Agent 365 and Microsoft Admin Center, and may use SharePoint content and site context for conversational experiences.
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. .agent file experiences transitioning to Agent Builder continue to use SharePoint content and site context with Microsoft 365 integration and centralized controls.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Upgrade path dependent. No changes for upgrading to Agent Builder. Converting to a skill enables it to be used with the capabilities of Copilot in SharePoint.
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Agent Builder, Microsoft Admin Center and Agent 365 are the places where governance, management, and usage analysis are available for these new and upgraded agents. 
Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Agent 365 provides centralized controls. Review applicable platform controls for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Simplifying AI access: Introducing usage-based billing
item.description:
Updated October 16, 2026: We have updated the content and timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

The new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business combines everyday AI via user subscription license with Advanced AI via usage-based billing. Beginning in mid-November, usage-based billing will be included by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases for tenants that have Microsoft 365 Business Premium. For CSP customers, usage-based billing will be included by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases starting December 1, 2026. This phased approach makes it easier to access eligible usage-based AI experiences, including Copilot Cowork and other long-running, autonomous agentic capabilities, while reducing billing complexity and preserving flexibility to expand usage over time based on business needs.

You have been identified as a customer who may be affected by this phased rollout.

What is changing

  • With eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases: Beginning in mid-November, pay-as-you-go usage-based billing will be configured by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases for tenants that have Microsoft 365 Business Premium. Tenants without Microsoft 365 Business Premium will follow at a later date. 
    • For CSP customers, beginning December 1 pay-as-you-go usage-based billing will be configured by default with eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases.
  • If your organization does not already have the required pay-as-you-go Azure resources and/or spending policy, it will be created as part of the eligible purchase and product setup. 
  • The resulting spending policy will have a spending limit of 4,000 Copilot credits per user per month with charges based on actual usage.
  • Charges apply only when these experiences are used, subject to the usage controls and spending limits established by your administrator.
  • We will begin rolling out this change to eligible customers in supported markets. The change will not initially be available in Australia, Belgium, Brazil, France, Germany, India, Italy, Korea, Netherlands, Poland, Spain. We will provide additional information about availability in these markets when available. 

What is not changing

  • Your existing Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscription benefits and payment terms do not change.
  • Capabilities already included with your license remain included; this change adds a spending policy for eligible usage-based experiences.
  • If your organization already has a spending policy configured, the existing spending policy remains in place.

When this will happen

  • Mid-November 2026: Usage-based billing default-on will begin for eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made directly from Microsoft, including through Microsoft web and the Microsoft 365 admin center, for tenants that have Microsoft 365 Copilot Business Premium.
  • Future rollout: Tenants that do not have Microsoft 365 Business Premium, including tenants that only have Microsoft 365 Business Standard and/or Basic with Copilot, or only Microsoft 365 Copilot Business.
  • Starting December 1, 2026: The change applies to eligible new Microsoft 365 Copilot Business purchases made through Cloud Solution Provider (CSP) channels.

How usage-based billing works

  • If your organization does not already have the required pay-as-you-go Azure resource and/or spending policy, it will be created as part of the eligible purchase and product setup.
  • Administrators can review and manage usage controls and spending policy in Cost Management in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Edge: Browser-native XSLT will be disabled by default
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft Edge is deprecating browser-native Extensible Stylesheet Language Transformations (XSLT). Edge will disable the XSLTProcessor JavaScript API and XML processing instructions that reference XSLT stylesheets by default. XML processing instructions that reference CSS stylesheets are not affected.

The native XSLT implementation depends on an aging native codebase that processes untrusted XML and XSLT content. Removing this functionality reduces the browser attack surface. XSLT also has low modern web usage, and safer migration alternatives are available.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Organizations may be affected if internal websites, public websites, embedded-device interfaces, or third-party web applications depend on browser-native XSLT. In Microsoft Edge 159, browser-native XSLT will be off by default in Stable. The temporary XSLTEnabled policy is planned for removal in Microsoft Edge 176 in Summer 2027.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

Before Microsoft Edge Stable 159, identify applications that use the XSLTProcessor JavaScript API or XML processing instructions that reference XSL stylesheets. To check for browser-native XSLT usage with Lighthouse in Microsoft Edge:

  1. Open the application in a current version of Microsoft Edge.
  2. Sign in and navigate to the application page you want to test.
  3. Open Edge DevTools with F12 or Ctrl+Shift+I.
  4. Select the Lighthouse tool. If it isn't visible, select More tools (+) > Lighthouse.
  5. Select:
    • Mode: Navigation
    • Category: Best Practices
  6. For authenticated applications: In Lighthouse Settings, turn off Clear storage so the audit preserves your signed-in session. Leave it enabled for public pages that don't require stored application state.
  7. Select Analyze page load.
  8. In the report:
    • Search for XSLT, deprecated, or XSLTProcessor.
    • Check for Uses deprecated APIs.
    • Expand Issues were logged in the DevTools Issues panel.
  9. Check the DevTools Issues and Console tools for XSLT deprecation warnings.
  10. Repeat the audit for each relevant page and exercise important application workflows.

Migrate affected applications to supported alternatives or contact the developers/vendor responsible for the affected site to update the application and remove its dependency on browser-native XSLT. If more time is needed, configure the temporary XSLTEnabled policy while application owners complete migration.

[Compliance considerations:]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control?Yes. Admins can temporarily use the XSLTEnabled policy to manage XSLT behavior while migrating affected applications.
Does the change modify or disable a capability?Yes. Browser-native XSLT will be disabled by default and the temporary policy is planned for removal in a future Edge release.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Facilitator proactively detects and resolves knowledge gaps in meetings
item.description:

[What and Why]

We are introducing a new Microsoft Teams Facilitator capability that proactively detects and resolves knowledge gaps during meetings. Facilitator can identify when participants ask questions or express uncertainty and retrieve and share relevant answers using web search in the meeting chat. This enhancement helps improve meeting productivity by reducing interruptions and enabling teams to stay focused on goals while accessing needed information. If a participant asks a factual question and no one responds, Facilitator can provide an answer directly in the meeting chat.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 558341.

[Rollout Schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning early December 2026 (previously early November) and expected to complete mid-December 2026 (previously mid-November)
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning mid-December 2026 (previously mid-November) and expected to complete mid-January 2027 (previously mid-December 2026)

[Impact on Your Organization]

Who is affected

  • Users in Microsoft Teams meetings where Facilitator is enabled with Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium)

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Teams (meetings)
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

  • Facilitator will monitor meeting conversations in real time to detect implicit or explicit information needs.
  • When a knowledge gap is identified, Facilitator performs a web search and posts a response in the meeting chat: 
  • Responses are infrequent in practice and typically occur less than once per meeting.
  • Responses are limited to questions relevant to the meeting discussion based on agenda signals and conversational context.
  • Facilitator must be manually added to the meeting and is not enabled by default.
  • A user with a Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) license must enable Facilitator for the meeting. Other participants do not need to be licensed to receive responses.
  • Admins can disable Facilitator at the tenant level. The feature depends on the Copilot web search setting. If web search is disabled, responses are not generated.
  • Users can stop the behavior at any time by removing Facilitator from the meeting.
  • The feature is supported in standard Teams meetings only and not supported in calls, webinars, or town halls.
  • The experience is supported in meetings that include external or cross-tenant participants.

[Action Required/Recommendations]

No immediate action is required.

Recommended actions:

  • Review your organization’s Copilot web search and Facilitator configuration settings to confirm alignment with your policies.
  • Inform helpdesk and users about proactive Facilitator responses in meeting chats.
  • Update internal documentation or training materials if you reference Teams meeting experiences.

[Compliance considerations]

Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI or machine learning capabilities that interact with customer data?Yes. Facilitator uses AI to interpret meeting content and generate contextual responses during meetings.
Does the change provide end users with a new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users receive proactive, AI-generated responses within the Teams meeting chat without needing to prompt the system.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through configuration settings?Yes. The feature depends on the Copilot web search setting, which admins can enable or disable to control functionality.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Improved file sharing experience in external chats
item.description:
Updated October 15, 2026: We are still finalizing rollout dates. Please update your settings by the first week of November to avoid any interruption. We will announce via Message center when we are ready to proceed. We apologize for the inconvenience. 

[What and why]

We’re improving the file-sharing experience in Microsoft Teams external (federated) chats by making the Attach file (paperclip) and drag-and-drop experiences available by default. This change only impacts tenants who have not adjusted the policy that controls file attachment in an external Teams chat. To opt out of this change, disable the capability using the Teams PowerShell setting provided in the “Action required and recommendations” section below. This can be done before the rollout and your policy setting will be respected. This update does not change your OneDrive or SharePoint external-sharing settings or override existing access restrictions. 

Prior to this change, when existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies allow, users can already share files in external chats by sharing a link to the file. This update makes that flow easier by adding the Attach file (paperclip) and drag-and-drop experiences directly in Teams. Files uploaded from the user’s device are stored in the sender’s OneDrive, while cloud files remain stored in their existing location. Teams then assigns permissions to chat participants, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint sharing policies. Senders can still review, modify, or remove file access before sending the message. This reduces the need to assign permissions manually, while allowing senders to stay in control.

  • More info: Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: We will announce via Message center when we are ready to proceed.
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will announce via Message center when we are ready to proceed.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Teams external access (federation)
  • This change applies only to organizations where the setting has not been explicitly configured. Any customers who have left the configuration in the default state will be impacted. 
  • Users participating in external 1:1 chats, external group chats, and meeting chats

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • External (federated) 1:1 chats
  • External (federated) group chats
  • Meeting chats
  • Teams desktop app
  • Teams web app

What will happen

  • The ability for users to attach and share files in external chats will be enabled for all Microsoft 365 tenants, unless your organization has previously explicitly disabled this setting in Teams. Any customers who have left the configuration in the default state will be impacted.
  • Users can already paste file links into external chants. This ability is unchanged. With this change, users will also have the ability to attach and share files using the paperclip option or drag and drop in external (federated) chats.
  • Files shared through these experiences continue to be stored and shared through OneDrive or SharePoint. Files uploaded from a user’s device are stored in the sender’s OneDrive, while existing cloud files remain in their current location. 
  • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams assigns permissions to participants in the external chat for files uploaded using paperclip or drag-and-drop, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies.
  • Senders can review, modify, or remove sharing permissions before sending a file.
  • Senders can continue to modify or revoke access after a file has been shared.
  • Automatic permission assignment applies only to files shared through the paperclip or drag-and-drop experience.
  • The files will be shared as hyperlinks after send. 
  • Existing OneDrive and SharePoint sharing controls continue to govern access.
  • Existing sensitivity labels, domain restrictions, and security protections continue to apply.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required to preserve external-sharing restrictions already configured in OneDrive and SharePoint; this update does not change those restrictions. To review or change these controls, see Manage sharing settings for SharePoint and OneDrive in Microsoft 365. 

[To disable file attachments in external chats]

To opt out of this change, apply the following Teams PowerShell setting if you have not already explicitly configured this setting:

Set-CsTeamsFilesPolicy -Identity Global -FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers Disabled

Verify the setting:

Get-CsTeamsFilesPolicy | Select Identity, FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers

Recommended actions:

  • Review your SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft Entra external sharing configuration because these settings continue to govern what external recipients can access.
  • Inform helpdesk and support teams about the updated attachment experience and the distinction between Teams attachment controls and OneDrive/SharePoint access controls. 
  • Update user training and internal documentation as needed.
  • Communicate to users that:
    • They can attach files directly in chats with people outside the organization.
    • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams assigns chat participants access to files shared via paperclip icon, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies. Senders can review, modify, or remove access before sending.
    • Pasted file links retain their existing permissions.
    • Files uploaded to external chats are stored in the sender's OneDrive and display.

Optional configuration to allow attachments without automatic permission assignment:

To disable automatic permission assignment while continuing to allow file attachments in external chats:

Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity Global -AutoShareFilesInExternalChats Disabled

If automatic permission assignment is disabled, users may need to manually grant access to shared files before external recipients can open them.

Allow several hours for policy changes to propagate before users see the updated experience.

Learn more:

  • Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Uploaded files shared through Attach or drag-and-drop can automatically receive permissions for participants in external chats. Existing OneDrive and SharePoint controls continue to govern access. Uploaded files are stored in the sender’s OneDrive.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?Yes. The direct file-attachment experience in external (federated) chats becomes available by default; the existing ability to paste file links remains unchanged.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Admins can separately control Teams file attachments and automatic permission assignment through Teams PowerShell policies. OneDrive and SharePoint sharing settings continue to govern external file access.

item.title: [stayInformed] Power Platform – Deprecation of temporary authentication URLs for the Word Online (Business) connector
item.description:
On October 14, 2026, the Word Online (Business) connector will remove its dependency on temporary, pre-authorized download URLs. This change improves the security for file access in SharePoint and OneDrive scenarios by requiring authenticated access for generated document content.

How does this affect me?
After this change, connector actions will use authenticated access to retrieve files instead of unauthenticated download URLs. This will affect organizations using the Word Online (Business) connector in Power Automate, Power Apps, or related SharePoint and OneDrive scenarios. Additionally, makers and admins with flows or integrations that depend on unauthenticated temporary or pre-authorized download URLs returned by connector actions will also be affected by this.

With this change:
  • The connector will remove its dependency on temporary or pre-authorized download URLs.
  • Flows relying on the CreateWordFileWithContent returned URL as an unauthenticated direct download link may be impacted. It is recommended that customers should review any flows that depend on the returned URL for unauthenticated file access.
The following actions are not expected to introduce any breaking changes as these operations already retrieve content using authenticated access:
  • GetSchema
  • GetFile: The connector will retrieve content using authenticated access.
  • ConvertFile / GetFilePDF: The connector will use authenticated streaming instead of a pre-authorized download URL.
What action do I need to take?
To prepare for this change, admins, users, and makers need to perform the following actions:
  • Use authenticated file content retrieval or appropriate SharePoint sharing links instead of unauthenticated download URLs.
  • Review flows and integrations that use Word Online (Business) connector to output URLs for unauthenticated file access.
  • For file-content scenarios, use SharePoint or OneDrive Get file content and pass the file content or bytes downstream.
  • For email attachment scenarios, use Get file content and then send the email with the file attached.
  • For sharing-link scenarios, use file metadata and create an appropriate SharePoint sharing link that matches your tenant and site sharing policies.
  • For HTTP, custom connector, Azure Function, or external service scenarios, ensure the downstream caller authenticates to SharePoint or Microsoft Graph and has permission to access the file.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Entra: Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors
item.description:
Updated October 13, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Entra will soon recognize Windows Hello for Business (WHfB) and macOS Platform Single Sign-On (PSSO) as standalone multifactor authentication (MFA) factors in supported authentication scenarios.

Today, WHfB and macOS PSSO can satisfy MFA requirements during primary sign-in, but users may still be required to register and use an additional passkey or authentication method for certain step-up authentication prompts, Authentication Strength policies, and sign-in frequency checks.

After this rollout, users who authenticate with WHfB or macOS PSSO will be able to satisfy supported MFA requirements without registering an additional passkey. This change helps organizations expand the use of phishing-resistant authentication methods and reduce reliance on less secure authentication methods. As part of this change, a user's WHfB and macOS PSSO credentials will be displayed in My Security Info as auto-registered passkeys.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete in mid-December 2026 (previously late November)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Entra ID
  • Users who authenticate with Windows Hello for Business
  • Users who authenticate with macOS Platform SSO
  • Organizations using Conditional Access Authentication Strength policies

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Windows Hello for Business
  • macOS Platform SSO
  • Conditional Access
  • Authentication Strength policies

What will happen

After rollout:

  • Users signing in with WHfB or macOS PSSO can complete supported MFA challenges without requiring a separate passkey.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO will satisfy supported MFA requirements for step-up authentication scenarios.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO can be used during 2FA to satisfy supported Authentication Strength policy requirements.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO can be used during 2FA to satisfy supported sign-in frequency challenge requirements.
  • Users whose only MFA method is WHfB or macOS PSSO will be considered MFA-capable.
  • Users who sign in with only a password will no longer be automatically prompted to register an additional MFA method if WHfB or macOS PSSO is their only registered MFA credential.
  • Users with WHfB or macOS PSSO credentials, will be able to see them listed in My Security Info as auto-registered passkeys.

[Action required and recommendations]

No configuration changes are required.

We recommend reviewing user onboarding and MFA registration processes before rollout. Because WHfB and macOS PSSO credentials are device-bound, users may not be able to complete MFA challenges from devices where those credentials are not available.

Recommended actions:

  • Update onboarding guidance to ensure users register at least one portable MFA method.
  • Consider requiring users to register a synced passkey or Microsoft Authenticator passkey in addition to WHfB or macOS PSSO.
  • Review custom Authentication Strength policies to confirm WHfB and macOS PSSO are allowed where appropriate.
  • Update user documentation because users with only WHfB or macOS PSSO registered will no longer be automatically guided to register an additional MFA method.

Learn more (To be updated closer to GA rollout.)

  • Plan a Windows Hello for Business deployment | Security | Windows | Microsoft Learn
  • Prepare users to provision and use Windows Hello for Business | Security | Windows | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Schedule prompts in Agent Builder
item.description:

[Introduction]

We’re introducing the ability to create workflows that schedule prompts in Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 Copilot. This new capability allows users to schedule prompts that run automatically on a defined cadence, such as hourly, daily, or weekly. Based on customer feedback requesting more automation and proactive insights, workflows help users reduce manual prompting and automate routine tasks using their Copilot agents.

[When this will happen]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout is expected to begin end of October 2026 (previously early September) and complete by end of November 2026 (previously end of September).

[How this affects your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who create and manage agents using Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium)

What will happen

  • Users will be able to create scheduled workflows for agents.
  • Scheduled workflows include:
    • Prompt text
    • Triggers and recurrence patterns
    • Date, time, and time zone settings
  • Supported recurrence patterns:
    • Hourly
    • Daily
    • Weekly
    • Monthly
    • Yearly
  • Workflows are configured per user and run only for the user who created them.
  • Workflows are not shared when an agent is shared with others.
  • Scheduled workflows will not run for draft or unpublished agents.
  • Users can view, edit, preview, and delete workflows within Agent Builder.
  • This feature is enabled by default and respects existing tenant and Copilot policies.

Screenshot of Agent Builder showing a “Project Horizon” agent configuration screen. The instructions panel is visible in the center, while a dropdown menu in the top-right corner is expanded with options including “Create a workflow for this agent” and “Manage workflows.” A purple arrow highlights the option to create a new workflow.

 

Screenshot of Agent Builder showing a “Project Horizon” agent configuration screen. A modal titled “Create a workflow to prompt your agent” is centered, with a text field labeled “Prompt” and scheduling options set to run weekly on Friday at 1:30 PM. A purple arrow highlights where to enter the prompt. 

[What you can do to prepare]

  • Consider informing users who build Copilot agents about the availability of workflows.
  • Update internal documentation or training materials if you support Copilot agent creation.
  • For privacy or compliance requests, continue using the existing Data Subject Request (DSR) processes.

Learn more: Dsr Compliance - Delete Flow | Dsr Compliance | Power Platform API | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does this change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Existing customer data may be processed automatically based on a time-based trigger rather than direct user initiation. The scope of data access remains unchanged and follows existing permissions.
Does this change introduce or significantly modify AI, ML, or agent capabilities that interact with customer data?Yes. This change introduces a new agent capability that allows Copilot agents to run prompts automatically on a defined schedule, instead of only responding to manual prompts.
Does this change provide a new way for users to interact with generative AI?Yes. Users can now interact with generative AI asynchronously through scheduled workflows that execute prompts on their behalf.
Can users enable or disable this feature themselves?Yes. Users can create, edit, disable, or delete scheduled workflows for their agents at any time.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Planner: AI-generated status reports in Planner Agent

[What and why]

We are introducing AI-generated status reports in Planner Agent. This feature uses Planner plan data to generate a status report that summarizes overall status, progress, risks, and next steps. Users can customize reports by specifying items such as audience, tone, length, reporting period, and report sections before reviewing and refining the generated content.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): Rollout has completed.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in late October 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations who have Planner agent enabled as part of the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.
  • Within those organizations, users with an active Microsoft 365 Copilot license who use Planner Agent.
    • Note: Users who view or edit reports do not require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license; a Copilot license is required only to generate reports.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Planner
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

  • Planner Agent will be able to generate AI-powered status reports from Planner plan data within Microsoft 365 Copilot app.
  • Reports will be generated only from Planner content that users already have permission to access. Existing Planner sharing permissions, Copilot policies, and agent controls continue to apply.
  • Reports will synthesize plan information, including tasks, owners, due dates, status, buckets, and recent activity, into sections such as executive summary, progress, risks and blockers, achievements, milestones, and next steps.
  • Users can customize reports by reporting period, sections, tone, length, audience, and additional instructions before reviewing and refining the generated content.
  • Reports can be exported to a Copilot Page and shared by link or exported to Word and PDF.
  • This feature adds new functionality and does not replace existing Planner capabilities.

Copilot-generated status report

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you:

  • Confirm that intended users have an active Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • Review Planner Agent and Copilot agent availability and settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center. If needed, the agent can be blocked tenant-wide.
  • Inform support teams and users about the new status report generating capability, which can be accessed via the Planner Agent in Copilot or the Reports tab in Planner.
    • Note that generating a report requires a plan that is shared with a Microsoft 365 Group and contains sufficient task data.
  • Update internal documentation, training, and change management materials as appropriate.

[Compliance considerations]

To assist our customers with identifying compliance concerns, review the questions below and provide details for impact if appropriate:

  • Does the change store new customer data?
    • [Answer] Yes. A status report generated from your plan appears in the Microsoft 365 Copilot conversation. If a user chooses to export it, the report is also saved as a copilot page or a word document.
  • Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (e.g., documents, emails, chats, etc.)?
    • [Answer] Yes. When an authorized user requests a report, Planner Agent uses information from a plan they can access to create a status report. If the user attaches a file as a template, that file will also be used for the request. This change does not edit the source plan or its tasks.
  • Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?
    • [Answer] Yes. It adds the ability to generate and refine a status report through Planner Agent chat using accessible plan information. It does not grant the agent access to plans the requesting user cannot access.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Entra: Changes to AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager permission for agent identities
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft Entra Agent ID is enforcing tighter restrictions for autonomous creation of an agent’s own identities. Currently, all agents are granted AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager upon creation without administrator approval. Starting November 4, Microsoft Entra will no longer automatically grant AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager to agent blueprint principals, and creation of identities will need an admin to grant consent.

Agents that use app-only authentication to create their own agent identities must be explicitly granted the AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager Microsoft Graph application permission or move to another supported authorization model before enforcement reaches their tenant.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Entra 
  • No action is required if your organization doesn't have an agent that depends on the automatic AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager grant.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra

What will happen

Today, an agent blueprint principal is granted AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager automatically. This implicit grant allows the principal to create agent identities without a tenant-admin granting an app-role assignment.

After enforcement, an administrator must grant the Microsoft Graph application permission AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager to agents that needs this authority.

This change:

  • Makes app-only agent identity creation authority visible, auditable, and revocable.
  • Makes AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager revocable if consented
  • Affects existing and future agents.
  • Doesn't remove existing agent identities or agent blueprints.
  • Doesn't remove the ability for agent identity blueprints to create agent identities, when AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager is explicitly granted by an administrator
  • Doesn't affect an agent that uses a directory role to authorize creation of agent identities.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required if your organization doesn't have an agent that depends on the automatic AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager grant.

Identify agents that create agent identities without a signed-in user.

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Go to Entra ID>Audit Logs.
  3. Set the Category to "ApplicationManagement"
  4. Set the Activity filter to "Add Service Principal"

Find events where the Initiated By (actor) Type is Application and the Target is an agent identity.

For each affected agent:

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Go to Entra ID>Agent blueprints>Search for your agent blueprint>Granted permissions
  3. Review if the Agent has any other granted permissions that may allow for creation of agent identities. If there are no other permissions allowing for creation, this agent relies on AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager.
  4. Starting October 16, you may grant the explicit AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager Microsoft Graph application permission through tenant-wide admin consent or manual app-role creation. Granting it earlier will cause an error. A successful grant appears in the Granted Permissions table with “An administrator” in the Granted By column.
  5. Test app-only agent identity creation before enforcement begins.
  6. Update operational guidance for a failed request after enforcement.

If an app-only request relies only on the automatic grant after enforcement reaches your tenant, the request will fail with a 403 authorization error.

Learn more

  • For more about how to grant your agents access to resources, visit Grant agents access to Microsoft 365 resources | Microsoft Learn. 
  • For the Microsoft Graph permission reference on AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager, visit Microsoft Graph permissions reference - Microsoft Graph | Microsoft Learn.

[Compliance considerations]

No specific compliance impacts have been identified for this configuration update.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Agent 365: Expanded access to Microsoft agent usage and activity insights in Microsoft 365 admin center

This change is limited to observability metrics. It does not remove licensing requirements for other Agent 365 capabilities or for agent activity metrics for agents built on third-party platforms.

Platforms and services

What will happen

  • An Agent 365 license will no longer be required to view usage and activity metrics for supported agents built by Microsoft or on Microsoft platforms.

  • In Registry, the affected usage and activity columns are Active users, Total sessions, Exception rate, and Run Time.
  • In Agent overview, affected cards and charts include Active users, Active users over time, and Trending agents by active users. These views may already be visible in organizations without an Agent 365 license. Reported values and trends may change temporarily as activity data accumulates during rollout.

  • As the change reaches your organization, some metrics may initially appear lower or show incomplete trends while activity data is collected. This temporary change does not necessarily indicate reduced agent usage.
  • Allow up to 30 days after data collection begins for a full 30-day reporting view for each enabled agent or platform. Completing the rollout does not mean every agent will immediately have a full 30-day history.
  • Data availability continues to depend on the agent or platform sending activity data and on applicable observability settings.
  • Existing licensing and access requirements for third-party agent observability are unchanged.
  • Other licensed Agent 365 capabilities, including risk-related features, continue to require the applicable license.

[Action required and recommendations]

When comparing usage before and after rollout, account for the time required to collect a full reporting window rather than interpreting a lower displayed value alone as a decline in usage.

Review the affected Microsoft 365 admin center views as the change reaches your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Dynamics 365 Apps - Add users without licenses to activity recipient fields (preview)
item.description:
We are announcing the ability to enable active Microsoft Entra users without Dataverse or Power Apps licenses as activity recipients. Created user records remain disabled and do not grant Dynamics 365 app access. This feature will reach public preview on October 15, 2026.

How does this affect me?
With this feature enabled, active Entra ID users who do not have a valid Dynamics 365 or Power Apps license can be selected in fields such as:
  • Email: To, Cc, and Bcc
  • Appointment: Owner, Required Attendees, and Optional Attendees
  • Phone call: Owner, Call From, and Call To
  • Task: Owner (co-owner)
What action do I need to take?
This message is for awareness, and no action is required.

If you would like more information on this feature, please visit Add users without licenses to activity recipient fields (preview).

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot for Outlook: New Copilot entry point in Classic Outlook
item.description:
Updated October 13, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We are updating the entry point for Copilot in Outlook to be more visually appealing and consistent. Located next to the Outlook ribbon, the Copilot entry point makes it easier for users to discover and use Copilot as they work. In addition to chat, it also surfaces contextual, AI-powered recommendations based on the task at hand, such as reading email, composing messages, or managing a calendar. With a single click, users can act on these suggestions to quickly summarize content, draft responses, organize information, and accomplish tasks more efficiently. The experience is designed to bring relevant Copilot capabilities closer to the user's workflow while providing a consistent Copilot experience across Microsoft 365 applications.

This update is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 567007.

[Rollout schedule]

General Availability 

  • Worldwide: Beginning late October 2026 (previously mid-October) and expected to complete by mid-November 2026 (previously early November)
  • GCC and GCC High: Beginning mid-November 2026 (previously early November) and expected to complete by early December 2026 (previously late November)
  • DoD: Beginning mid-November 2026 (previously early November) and expected to complete by early December 2026 (previously late November)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • All users with Copilot license and enterprise license users (with or without Copilot license) will see the new DAB.

Platforms and services

  • Classic Outlook for Windows
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

  • The entry point for Copilot in classic Outlook will be updated and located next to the Outlook ribbon: 
  • Users will continue to have access to the Copilot side pane.
  • This new entry point will surface contextual, AI-powered recommendations based on the task at hand.
  • The feature will be available by default for eligible users with the required Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • No existing Copilot licensing requirements or admin settings are changing as part of this update.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required.

We recommend that you:

  • Inform users that the Copilot entry point in classic Outlook is moving to a new location.
  • Update any internal documentation or training materials that reference the current location of the Copilot button.
  • Communicate the change to help desk and support teams so they can assist users when the new experience becomes available.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft Purview: permissions audit log improvements
item.description:
Updated October 13, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

To improve transparency and troubleshooting for Microsoft Purview role-based access control (RBAC), we are enhancing audit logging for permission checks performed in the Microsoft Purview portal. These new audit records will provide administrators with clearer visibility into role and scoped-role authorization decisions, helping them investigate access issues and better understand how access evaluations are performed.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 569363.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in late September 2026 and expected to complete by late October 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Purview administrators and compliance administrators who review audit logs for access investigations and troubleshooting

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview portal
  • Microsoft Purview Audit

What will happen

  • New audit records will be generated when access checks are performed in the Microsoft Purview portal.
  • Two new audit operations will be available:
    • CheckUsersInRoles
    • CheckUserInRolesWithScopes
  • Administrators will be able to review these audit records as part of SecurityComplianceRBAC audit activities.
  • The enhancement is enabled by default and requires no configuration.
  • Audit records will only be generated for access checks that occur after the feature is deployed.
  • No historical or retroactive audit records will be created for prior access checks.
  • There is no impact for organizations.
  • Supported permission-assignment and role-group change audit records will include the ClientPortal field within PreExecutionMessage, helping administrators distinguish changes initiated from Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Defender. 
    • Supported activities for portal attribution 
      • Permission assignments: Granting, updating, or removing permission assignments. 
      • Role groups: Creating, updating, or deleting role groups. 
  • Expected ClientPortal values: 
    • Microsoft Purview portal: "ClientPortal": "Microsoft Purview" 
    • Microsoft Defender portal: "ClientPortal": "Microsoft Defender" 
    • Missing or unrecognized X-ClientPage value: "ClientPortal": "Unknown"

RBAC audit-CheckUserInRolesWithScopes:

RBAC audit-checkusersinroles:

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that administrators:

  • Review internal monitoring and audit procedures to determine whether the new audit activities should be included in access investigations.
  • Inform compliance and security teams about the availability of the new audit operations.
  • Update any internal documentation or reporting processes that reference Microsoft Purview RBAC audit data.

Learn more

  • Permissions in the Microsoft Purview portal | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable audit logging capabilities?Yes. The change enhances audit logging capabilities by adding two new audit operations.
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Yes. Administrators gain additional audit visibility into RBAC access evaluation outcomes, improving monitoring and troubleshooting capabilities.
